findings.title: Dry run can write through absolute symlinks into real files
findings.description: `copyInstallPaths` preserves symlinks when copying install paths into the sandbox. If a copied path is an absolute symlink (for example, `.claude/rules` pointing outside the sandbox), the installer can follow it and modify files at the symlink’s real destination. That breaks the `--dry-run` guarantee that nothing is written. Reject or safely dereference symlinks before running the installer in the sandbox, and add a regression test.

findings.title: Dry-run failures discard the diagnostics explaining them
findings.description: The install’s stdout is buffered, but buffered lines are replayed only after `install(...)` returns successfully. If the install aborts after printing a diagnostic—for example, because managed-section markers are broken—the exception skips replay, and the outer installer returns failure without showing that explanation. Replay relevant buffered diagnostics when the install throws as well.
